extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent practitioners, and others involved in filing or prosecuting U.S. patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to file an Information Disclosure Statement (IDS) during U.S. patent prosecution, including phase-specific timing, fee and statement requirements under 37 C.F.R. § 1.97, and the QPIDS program after payment of the issue fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose material information
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors, patent practitioners, and other individuals associated with filing and/or prosecuting a patent application have a duty to disclose to the USPTO all information known to be 'material' in determining patentability. This duty is ongoing throughout pendency of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuously monitor for material references or information during the entire prosecution and ensure timely submission via IDS when material information is discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of an IDS
rubrics_metrics.description: The mechanism to submit 'material' information to the USPTO is an information disclosure statement (IDS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an IDS to formally notify the Examiner of material prior art or other material information so it will be considered in determining patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for IDS consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS must be timely filed in order for the information to be officially considered by the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the phase-specific timing rules in 37 C.F.R. § 1.97 to ensure the Examiner will consider submitted information; late submissions may require additional procedures or fees to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 1 IDS timing and fee rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An Applicant may file an IDS within three months after the U.S. filing date, before the mailing of a first office action on the merits, or before the mailing of a first office after the filing of a request for continued examination (RCE). No fees are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where possible, file within Phase 1 (within three months of US filing or before first office action) to avoid fees and maximize likelihood of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 2 IDS timing and fee/statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: After phase 1 (e.g., once an office action has issued), an Applicant may file an IDS provided that it is before the mailing of a final office action, a notice of allowance, or an Ex-parte Quayle action. At this phase, the Applicant must pay a fee or submit a statement under 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) that the cited information was (1) first cited in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months before filing of the IDS, or (2) not cited in a foreign counterpart application and to the knowledge of the person making the statement, not known to any individual with the duty of disclosure more than three months before filing of the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filing during Phase 2, either pay the required IDS fee or carefully prepare and rely on a 1.97(e) statement meeting one of the two specified conditions to avoid fees; ensure the statement's factual bases are defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) statement conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement under 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e) may be used instead of paying a fee in certain situations: (1) the cited information was first cited in a counterpart foreign application not more than three months before filing the IDS, or (2) the cited information was not cited in a foreign counterpart application and, to the knowledge of the person making the statement, was not known to any individual with the duty of disclosure more than three months before filing the IDS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify timing and knowledge-conditions before signing a 1.97(e) statement; improper statements can be problematic. The same statement requirement appears for later-phase filings (Phase 3 and QPIDS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase 3 IDS timing and requirement (issue fee stage)
rubrics_metrics.description: After phase 2, an Applicant can only file an IDS before or with the payment of the issue fee together with a fee and a statement under 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e). If a statement cannot be made, the Applicant must file an RCE to have the information in the IDS considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material information arises late (after Phase 2), either provide the 1.97(e) statement and pay the fee when paying the issue fee, or file an RCE to have the Examiner consider the IDS; plan to avoid issuing an invalid patent due to undisclosed material information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quick Path Information Disclosure Statement (QPIDS) after issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If material information comes to light after the payment of the issue fee, an Applicant may file an IDS under the Quick Path Information Disclosure Statement (QPIDS) program if it is possible to make the statement under 37 C.F.R. § 1.97(e). The QPIDS program allows an Applicant to avoid the delay and cost of an RCE otherwise needed to obtain consideration of an IDS after payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use QPIDS when appropriate to avoid an RCE: QPIDS requires submitting a petition to withdraw the application from issue and a conditional RCE with the associated RCE fee; if the Examiner, after considering the IDS, finds the application remains allowable, the RCE will not be entered and the RCE fee returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: QPIDS procedural requirements and conditional RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: The QPIDS requirements include submitting a petition to withdraw the application from issue and a conditional RCE with the associated RCE fee. A conditional RCE means that if the application remains allowable after consideration of the IDS, the examiner will acknowledge consideration of the IDS, and will not enter the RCE and return the RCE fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the petition and conditional RCE correctly; understand that QPIDS acceptance depends on the ability to make the 1.97(e) statement and Examiner handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-material or cumulative information not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Information that is not material to patentability of the claims and/or cumulative to the information already of record is not required to be submitted to the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise judgment to avoid submitting immaterial or duplicative references; unnecessary submissions can clutter the file and incur costs without benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical recommendation — file as soon as possible
rubrics_metrics.description: It is recommended to file an IDS as soon as possible to make sure all information will be considered and to avoid any additional costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early disclosure (Phase 1 when possible) avoids fees, procedural complications, and reduces risk of later accusations of withholding material information.
